title: Capture Tactics
subtitle: Beginner · 4 lessons
description: Learn to spot atari, run the ladder, and read the basic kill patterns that come up in every game.

lessons.title: Atari basics
lessons.summary: A stone with one liberty is in atari — one move from capture.

sections.body: A stone is in atari when it has exactly one liberty left. If your opponent fills that liberty, the stone is captured. Recognizing atari — both ways — is the first tactical skill of Go.

sections.caption: The white stone has one liberty (marked). Black plays there to capture.

sections.body: When you place a stone, scan around it for opponent stones in atari. If you can capture instead of defending, you almost always should — captured stones are gone forever and the resulting space becomes yours to use.

lessons.title: Extend or capture?
lessons.summary: When you're in atari, you can extend, run, or take the opponent first.

sections.body:
When your own stone is in atari, you have three options:

1. Extend — add a stone to give the group more liberties.
2. Capture — take an opponent stone whose capture would free your liberties.
3. Sacrifice — sometimes losing one stone is better than running into a losing fight.

Look for option 2 first. It often solves both problems with one move.

sections.caption: Two white stones with a single shared liberty. One move captures both.

lessons.title: Edges and corners
lessons.summary: Stones near the edge have fewer liberties — capture is often closer than it looks.

sections.body: A stone in the middle of the board has 4 liberties. On the edge it has only 3. In the corner, only 2. That means stones near the edge are in atari one move earlier — both yours and your opponent's.

sections.caption: The edge does half the work. Closing one liberty captures.

lessons.title: The corner
lessons.summary: Corners give the fewest liberties of all — and the cleanest kills.

sections.body: Corner stones are the most vulnerable on the board. Memorize this: a single corner stone needs three friends to live; two stones lined up need a careful eye-shape. Whenever a corner is involved, count the liberties carefully.

sections.caption: Two liberties around a corner stone. Close one and it's over.
